plate.viewWhy: The parallel torso, the hinge and the bar end rising to the chest are front-to-back (c3, c6); the census draws it side.
plate.equipment: Landmine rig: barbell pinned at a floor pivot in front of the lifter, plates on the near free end; hands on the bar just below the plates (c1, c4). Needs the landmine composer (census gap).
plate.start: Facing the bar, feet shoulder width (c2), hips and knees bent, back straight, torso roughly parallel to the floor (c3), arms straight to the bar end (c8).
plate.end: Same torso angle; elbows driven back, bar end at the chest, shoulder blades squeezed together (c6).

checkpoints.label: Torso parallel
checkpoints.what: Back straight, torso roughly level with the floor.

checkpoints.label: Brace first
checkpoints.what: Trunk braced before each pull so the lower back doesn’t round.

checkpoints.label: Elbows back
checkpoints.what: Elbows drive back, bar to the chest.

mistake.what: Rounded lower back over the bar.
mistake.why: The anchor’s bracing and spine cues exist to stop it (c5, c9); on the landmine T-bar it is named one of the most common mistakes (c11), and the lift loads the lower back (c15).

grip.type: Overhand, both hands on the bar just below the plates.
grip.width: Close: both hands on the bar end.
grip.handContact: Bar across the base of the fingers and top of the palm (pull archetype).
grip.wrist: Straight in line with the forearm (pull archetype range); not curled.
